flags.text: The bank trap note on -4 is a substitution check ("Substituting -4 gives 10 on the left and 6 on the right"), not the route a student takes; the note here names the route (stopping at the coefficient). The bank why uses an arrow glyph.

routing: Works today: the anchor scrolls the QR engine to this skill section, with its pattern card, its picture and its worked examples. A first-visit tour opens on top (Skip closes it), and the section header reads LOCKED until its prerequisites are marked mastered, though everything in it still shows. The page also carries a timed simulator, a streak counter and mastery counts in its other views; the anchor lands on the section, not on those.

changes: The first dashed exit names the slip behind -6: x moved across without changing its sign, -3x + x, giving -2x - 2 = 10 (it said adding x, which done to both sides gives -2x - 2 = 2x + 10); the alt says the same

Re-review round 3, optional note taken: the -6 note runs one move at a time, "Adding x to -3x gives -2x - 2 = 10, then -2x = 12, so x = -6." (it went straight to -2x = 12, folding the x move and the 2 move into one); label and family unchanged

served.stem: What value of x satisfies -3x - 2 = x + 10?

answer.line: Collect x on one side and the numbers on the other: -4x = 12, so x = -3.

steps: Put the x terms on one side first. Subtract x from both sides: -4x - 2 = 10.
Then the numbers. Add 2 to both sides: -4x = 12.
Divide by -4: x = -3. A positive divided by a negative is negative.
Check it in the original: -3(-3) - 2 = 7 and -3 + 10 = 7. Both sides match.

choices.note: Adding x to -3x gives -2x - 2 = 10, then -2x = 12, so x = -6. To clear x off the right side, subtract it from both sides: -3x - x = -4x.
-4 is the number in front of x after collecting, -4x = 12. One move is left: divide 12 by -4.
Carrying the -2 across without changing its sign gives -4x = 10 - 2 = 8, so x = -2. Add 2 to both sides instead: 10 + 2 = 12.
The setup -4x = 12 is right, but 12 divided by -4 is -3. A positive over a negative comes out negative.

student.lockIt: Same move to both sides: x terms to one side, numbers to the other, then divide.

playWith.label: Linear Equations balance: pick 5x - 7 = 2x + 8 and keep both pans level one move at a time

exits.label: Move x across without changing its sign, -3x + x, and you get -2x - 2 = 10, which leads to -6.
Divide by 4 instead of -4 and the minus drops: you land on 3.
